text:
The Wild have points in 14 straight games (11-0-3), and Saturday's shootout loss in Vancouver only extended it. Their top line is the best thing in the league right now: Joel Eriksson Ek, Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy have outscored opponents 24-2 at 5-on-5 with 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes both pushed their point streaks to 13 games this week.

At 17-3-5, the record runs ahead of the play, but not by as much as you might think. Minnesota has a 56% share of expected goals overall. The gap is in net: the Wild have allowed about 16 fewer goals than their chances against predict. Jesper Wallstedt has not lost in November, and our standings model has them about seven points ahead of their play. Even giving all of that back, they are a good team.

The scare of the week was Hughes, who left Thursday's win in Calgary after a collision with a Flames forward. He has 16 points in his last 10 games, and his pair with Jared Spurgeon has taken 65% of the chances. Brock Faber, back after a skull fracture, scored in his first home game since the injury.

Our numbers give Minnesota a 99% playoff chance and 63% to win the Central. What we'd watch: Hughes's status, and whether the saves hold once the shooting cools.
